solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Urchin's game curtailed in funfair roundabout

indicators.note: in says the shortened word sits inside the rearranged letters
a roundabout goes round and round, so the letters of the word funfair are spun into a new order
a curtailed word has lost its tail, its last letter

parts.note: game taken as the plain word

explanation.surface: A street child's game is cut short on the merry-go-round at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' makes RAUFFIN; 'in' slots the shortened game in after its first two letters. The 's stands for 'is', a link, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both name a ragged, scruffy child of the streets.

clue.text: Skirt, one on Violet's something exceptional

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next one

parts.note: a ra-ra skirt is a short flounced skirt, so skirt gives RARA
one is A, as in a single thing
Vi is the short form of the name Violet, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Violet's skirt, worn with something else, is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: A rara avis is Latin for 'rare bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a rare bird, used in English for a person or thing that is unusually fine or unique.

clue.text: Worry over model railway framework

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to worry someone is to nag them
the Model T was the classic Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Anxiety about a model railway's supporting structure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' turns the word upside down, giving GAN; the Model T Ford supplies the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is an overhead structure of steel bars supporting signals, cranes or lights.

clue.text: New way ships follow

indicators.note: follow says the ships come after the word for way

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
RN is the Royal Navy, the fleet of British ships

explanation.surface: A novel route that ships take.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something up to date or recent is new.

clue.text: Right to sell that belonging to him in country

indicators.note: in says the pronoun is placed inside the country

parts.note: France is the country chosen
the possessive pronoun his means that which belongs to him

explanation.surface: A man's entitlement to trade what he owns within his own nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence granted to sell a company's goods or services under its name.

clue.text: Top cover for retirement?

parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, and the top cover is headwear worn there; the word also means a last drink before bed

explanation.surface: What covers you once you stop working?
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work; here it means retiring for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft cap worn in bed is literally a head covering for the hours of sleep.

clue.text: Accountant's Australian home

parts.note: a CA is a chartered accountant, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: The house belonging to an accountant from Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Casa is the Spanish and Italian word for a house, used in English for a dwelling.

clue.text: Leaves for twelve months

parts.note: the leaves are pages, one for each month of the year, not foliage or departures

explanation.surface: Someone goes away for a year, or a tree's foliage lasts all year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure or tree foliage; it is the pages of a wall chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall chart of dates has a page, or leaf, for each month of the year.

clue.text: Knots Lee extricated to reveal bones

indicators.note: untangling knots means pulling their strands into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Lee gets free of tied knots and his bones are exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The framework of bones of a body is its skeleton.

clue.text: Call and face timekeeper

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Phone and confront the person keeping time.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring dial is a portable sundial shaped like a ring, an old device for telling the hour.

clue.text: Kitchen garden walk that's good at the start

indicators.note: at the start puts the letter for good in front

parts.note: an alley is a path in a garden, often lined with trees

explanation.surface: A kitchen garden with a fine path at its entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cooking area on a ship or aircraft, and also a narrow cooking space at home.

clue.text: Might it be used in building cavity wall?

definitions.text: Might it be used in building cavity wall?

parts.words: Might it be used in building cavity wall?
parts.note: a cavity is filled with air and a wall is made of brick, and this vented block is indeed laid into such walls

explanation.surface: A builder's question about materials for a double-skinned wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An air brick is a perforated block set into a wall to let air circulate through its gap.

clue.text: Note apple coming from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left, backwards

parts.note: the rennet, or reinette, is a variety of dessert apple

explanation.surface: A fruit imported from Asia, with a message attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote worth ten pounds is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Jot first nine letters backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the phrase is read in reverse order

parts.note: the first nine letters of the alphabet run from A to I

explanation.surface: Scribble the alphabet's opening letters in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jot' looks like a verb meaning write; here it is the noun, a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean the smallest possible amount, from the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: Second person in Calais removed reptile from plant

parts.note: in French, spoken in Calais, the familiar second-person pronoun is tu

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are shifted out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in France took a snake away from a garden shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American tree of the magnolia family with tulip-shaped flowers.

clue.text: I have left continual prosperity

indicators.note: left means gone away, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: successive means following one after another, continual
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone has walked away from endless wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction; it is the past of 'leave', taking away I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of doing well: thriving, wealth and good fortune.

clue.text: Free of charge

parts.note: not costless, but a verb: to relieve someone of a load or burden

explanation.surface: Something given without cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'costing nothing'; read 'Free' as a verb and 'charge' as a load carried.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a load, worry or weight is to lift that weight from them.

clue.text: Over-confident birds on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the birds above the river

parts.note: cocks are male birds
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Arrogant birds strutting by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone overly sure of themselves is arrogantly self-assured.

clue.text: He minds when he has a job

definitions.text: He minds when he has a job

parts.words: He minds when he has a job
parts.note: minds means looks after, not objects; the job is tending a flock

explanation.surface: A man who gets annoyed when given work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minds' reads as 'objects to'; it means 'looks after', as a flock-keeper does.
explanation.definitionFit: The flock-keeper's job is to look after, or mind, sheep.

clue.text: Openly paid in advance

definitions.meaning: money handed over before goods or work arrive

explanation.surface: Money paid ahead of time, in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both candid and frank, and paid before delivery.

clue.text: Righted a wrong for mature students

indicators.note: putting the letters wrong means setting them out of order

explanation.surface: Older learners correct a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The University of the Third Age is a British movement offering learning to retired people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the active years after retirement, and so those older people who keep studying in them.

clue.text: Restore to good condition in the Alps

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Mend something while up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make sound or well again, as a wound or a rift.

clue.text: Rich man takes time to strip

parts.note: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus

explanation.surface: A wealthy man takes a moment to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to deprive or take off, as clothing or possessions.

clue.text: No German saying it's a drug

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter is left out

parts.note: stating is saying or declaring

explanation.surface: A German declares that something is a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No German' looks like 'nein'; it means without G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a class of drugs taken to lower cholesterol in the blood.

clue.text: Help in rising when bed-bound?

parts.note: not care for an invalid: a lift for someone climbing, and the bed is a bunk to get up into

explanation.surface: Assistance getting up when you are confined to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed-bound' suggests an invalid; it means heading for a top bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-up or boost given to someone climbing is British slang of this form.

clue.text: Chip off the old block

parts.note: the idiom means a child like a parent; read literally, it is a sliver broken from a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A child who resembles a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom points to family likeness; read literally it is a sliver of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp sliver broken off wood is literally a chip from a block.

clue.text: Cite present-day dictator

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era
Il Duce was the title of the dictator Mussolini

explanation.surface: Mention a modern tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to bring forward as evidence or quote an example.

clue.text: Free agent did not start mixing drink

indicators.note: mixing says the remaining letters are stirred into a new order
not starting means the first letter is lost

explanation.surface: An unattached sports player sat out the match, mixing cocktails instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an unfermented tea from China and Japan, drunk as a beverage.

clue.text: Only partly concerned in days past

indicators.note: only partly means just a portion of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Formerly someone was only slightly worried.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Amateur poet accepting new title

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the poet holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of title

explanation.surface: An unpaid versifier is given a fresh honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives ILETT, which 'accepting' places between the poet's first letter and the rest of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler who pursues an art for love rather than profession is an amateur.
